title: The $18,000 surprise: NAT gateway data processing
intro: Finance flags that 'EC2 - Other' jumped from $2k to $18k last month. No new instances were launched. The only notable change: the data team moved their nightly jobs, which read about 400TB a month from S3, into private subnets 'for security'.

steps.prompt: Break last month's (2026-08-01 to 2026-09-01) EC2 - Other cost down by usage type.
expected_commands: aws ce get-cost-and-usage --time-period Start=2026-08-01,End=2026-09-01 --granularity MONTHLY --metrics UnblendedCost --filter '{"Dimensions":{"Key":"SERVICE","Values":["EC2 - Other"]}}' --group-by Type=DIMENSION,Key=USAGE_TYPE
steps.hint: Group by USAGE_TYPE to see what's inside 'EC2 - Other'.

steps.prompt: Almost all of it is NAT gateway data processing ($0.045 per GB). The S3 reads from private subnets go out through the NAT. Check whether the VPC vpc-0f1e2d3c4b5a69788 has an S3 gateway endpoint.
steps.fake_output:
VpcEndpointId            ServiceName                            Type       State
vpce-0a1b2c3d4e5f60718   com.amazonaws.us-east-1.ssm            Interface  available
vpce-0b2c3d4e5f6071829   com.amazonaws.us-east-1.ssmmessages    Interface  available
steps.hint: S3 traffic can bypass the NAT only through a gateway endpoint for com.amazonaws.<region>.s3.

steps.prompt: There's no S3 endpoint. Create a gateway endpoint for com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 in vpc-0f1e2d3c4b5a69788, associated with the private route tables rtb-0e9d8c7b6a5f43210 and rtb-0f8e7d6c5b4a32109.
expected_commands: aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0f1e2d3c4b5a69788 --vpc-endpoint-type Gateway --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 --route-table-ids rtb-0e9d8c7b6a5f43210 rtb-0f8e7d6c5b4a32109
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0f1e2d3c4b5a69788 --service-name com.amazonaws.us-east-1.s3 --route-table-ids rtb-0e9d8c7b6a5f43210 rtb-0f8e7d6c5b4a32109
steps.hint: A gateway endpoint adds a route (an S3 prefix list) to each route table you name.

steps.prompt: Verify the route was added to the private route table rtb-0e9d8c7b6a5f43210.
steps.fake_output:
Destination            Target                   State
10.0.0.0/16            local                    active
pl-63a5400a            vpce-0c3d4e5f6071829a3   active
0.0.0.0/0              nat-0123456789abcdef0    active
steps.hint: Look for a pl-... destination (the S3 prefix list) pointing at the vpce-...

resolution: Moving the jobs into private subnets was a good security decision with an unplanned cost: every byte they read from S3 now left through the NAT gateway, which charges about $0.045 per GB processed, on top of its hourly fee. 400TB a month through a NAT is roughly $18,000. A gateway VPC endpoint for S3 (and DynamoDB) is free and routes that traffic privately inside AWS; route tables prefer the more specific S3 prefix-list route over 0.0.0.0/0, so the jobs needed no change. Lessons: add S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints to every VPC template by default; 'EC2 - Other' is where network costs hide, so break it down by usage type; and set AWS Budgets alerts on individual usage types, so a 9x jump is caught in days, not at month-end. Interface endpoints (for other services) are not free: compare them with NAT costs before adding them.
